meta.disclaimer: Guidance only, not medical advice. Confirm with a doctor or licensed blood bank before making clinical decisions.
meta.attribution: Guidelines consolidated from National Blood Transfusion Council (NBTC, MoHFW, Govt. of India), WHO, and Indian Red Cross Society.

O-.clinical_note: Universal red cell donor. Can ONLY receive O- negative blood.
O-.source: NBTC India Blood Transfusion Guidelines & WHO BTS

O+.clinical_note: Can receive O+ and O- red blood cells.
O+.source: NBTC India Blood Transfusion Guidelines & WHO BTS

A-.clinical_note: Can receive A- and O- red blood cells.
A-.source: NBTC India Blood Transfusion Guidelines & WHO BTS

A+.clinical_note: Can receive A+, A-, O+, and O- red blood cells.
A+.source: NBTC India Blood Transfusion Guidelines & WHO BTS

B-.clinical_note: Can receive B- and O- red blood cells.
B-.source: NBTC India Blood Transfusion Guidelines & WHO BTS

B+.clinical_note: Can receive B+, B-, O+, and O- red blood cells.
B+.source: NBTC India Blood Transfusion Guidelines & WHO BTS

AB-.clinical_note: Can receive all Rh-negative red blood cells (AB-, A-, B-, O-).
AB-.source: NBTC India Blood Transfusion Guidelines & WHO BTS

AB+.clinical_note: Universal red cell recipient. Can receive all standard ABO and Rh blood groups.
AB+.source: NBTC India Blood Transfusion Guidelines & WHO BTS

Bombay (Oh+).clinical_note: Extremely rare phenotype (lacks H-antigen). CANNOT receive O, A, B, or AB blood. Can ONLY receive Bombay Blood Group.
Bombay (Oh+).source: NBTC India Guidelines for Management of Rare Blood Groups

Bombay (Oh-).clinical_note: Ultra-rare Rh-negative Bombay phenotype. Can ONLY receive Bombay Oh- units.
Bombay (Oh-).source: NBTC India Guidelines for Management of Rare Blood Groups

age.description: Donors must be between 18 and 65 years of age.
age.source: Drugs & Cosmetics Act (Schedule F, Part XII-B) & NBTC India

weight.description: Minimum weight of 45 kg for 350 ml whole blood collection; 50 kg for 450 ml collection.
weight.source: NBTC India Blood Donor Selection Criteria

hemoglobin.description: Hemoglobin level must be at least 12.5 g/dL for both male and female donors.
hemoglobin.source: NBTC India Blood Donor Selection Criteria & WHO

donation_interval.description: Minimum interval between whole blood donations: 90 days (3 months) for males, 120 days (4 months) for females.
donation_interval.source: NBTC India Standards for Blood Banks and Blood Transfusion Services

vital_signs.description: Pulse 60-100 bpm regular, normal blood pressure without severe hypertension, afebrile.
vital_signs.source: NBTC India / Indian Red Cross Society Guidelines

temporary_deferrals.question: Have you consumed alcohol in the last 24 hours?
temporary_deferrals.reason: Alcohol can cause dehydration and temporary liver enzyme fluctuations.

temporary_deferrals.question: Have you gotten a tattoo, cosmetic piercing, or acupuncture in the last 12 months?
temporary_deferrals.reason: Risk of blood-borne viral transmission (Hepatitis B, C, HIV) during the window period.
temporary_deferrals.source: NBTC India Standards for Blood Banks (2020 revision)

temporary_deferrals.question: Have you undergone major surgery in the last 12 months or minor surgery in the last 6 months?
temporary_deferrals.reason: Allows full physiological recovery and tissue restoration post-operative stress.
temporary_deferrals.source: NBTC India Standards for Blood Banks

temporary_deferrals.question: Are you currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or have given birth within the last 12 months?
temporary_deferrals.reason: Protects maternal iron stores and infant nutrition.
temporary_deferrals.source: NBTC India & WHO Guidelines on Blood Donor Selection

temporary_deferrals.question: Are you currently taking antibiotics or recovering from an active infection/fever?
temporary_deferrals.reason: Wait at least 7 days after completing antibiotics and full resolution of symptoms.

temporary_deferrals.question: Have you received a live attenuated vaccine (e.g., MMR, Yellow Fever) in the last 4 weeks?
temporary_deferrals.reason: Prevents passive transmission of attenuated viral particles to immunocompromised recipients.
temporary_deferrals.source: WHO Guidelines on Blood Donor Selection
